paragraphs.text: By which is signified, that even though we are in great misery, yet there is always room for prayer.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: He declares that in our prayer we must lively feel that which we desire, and steadfastly believe to obtain.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: These excessive kinds of speech show how much the affliction of the Church should wound the hearts of the godly.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: My sorrows were so great that I did not eat.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Always mourning in solitude and casting out fearful cries.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: I have not risen out of my mourning to take my refreshment.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: He shows that not only the afflictions moved him, but chiefly the feeling of God's displeasure.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Though we are frail, yet your promise is sure, and the remembrance of it will confirm us forever.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: That is, the seventy years which by the prophet Jeremiah you appointed, Jer 29:12.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: The more the Church is in misery and desolation, the more the faithful should love and pity it.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: That is, when he will have drawn his church out of the darkness of death.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: The deliverance of the Church is an excellent benefit, and therefore he compares it to a new creation for in their banishment the body of the Church seemed to have been dead, which by deliverance was as it were created anew.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: Who now in their banishment could look for nothing but death.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: He shows that Gad's name is never more praised, than when religion flourishes and the church increases: which is chiefly accomplished under the kingdom of Christ.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: The church lament that they see not the time of Christ, which was promised, but have but few years and short days.
paragraphs.label: q

paragraphs.text: If heaven and earth perish, much more man will perish: but the Church by reason of God's promise endures forever.
paragraphs.label: r

paragraphs.text: Seeing you have chosen your Church out of the world, and joined it to you, it cannot but continue forever: for you are everlasting.
